strategy.summary: Reproduce the cephes.yn large-order overflow: on the buggy revision the yn loop runs past the point where the accumulated value becomes infinite and returns NaN instead of -inf; on the fixed revision the added isfinite(an) termination returns -inf. Build SciPy from the buggy commit a24f7847e8cc (editable/in-tree build so the compiled cephes extension reflects the C source), then run the regression test test_yn_gh_20405 in scipy/special/tests/test_basic.py. The test asserts exact equality observed == -np.inf, so it fails on buggy (NaN != -inf) and passes on fixed.

system_packages: gcc or clang with C/C++ toolchain
gfortran (required by SciPy build for some modules)
pinned_because: SciPy: documented constraint is null in the evidence, so the source tree itself defines the build; the build must be from the buggy commit so the cephes C code is the one under test
NumPy: no documented constraint and no era table entry; choose the NumPy version that the buggy commit's build requirements (pyproject.toml) resolve to, unpinned otherwise

strategy.reproducing_test:
def test_yn_gh_20405(self):
    # Enforce correct asymptotic behavior for large n.
    observed = cephes.yn(500, 1)
    assert observed == -np.inf
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision a24f7847e8cc the test fails: cephes.yn(500, 1) returns NaN and the equality with -np.inf is False, so the assertion fails. On the fixed revision (the PR with while (k < n && isfinite(an)) in cephes/yn.c) the test passes because cephes.yn(500, 1) returns -inf exactly.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "from scipy.special import cephes; import numpy as np; print(cephes.yn(500,1), cephes.yn(500,1)==-np.inf)"
risks: The failing transition is in the cephes yn C loop; the yv path (Amos Fortran-to-C translation in amos.h) is a separate code path and the regression test does not exercise it, so passing test_yn_gh_20405 does not verify the yv(300,1) fix.
Exact equality to -np.inf is required; any tolerance-based check would not detect the bug, so the test must be run as written.

Amos unk2 changes in amos.h are platform-independent C, but results for large order may depend on compiler optimisation and floating-point flags (e.g. -ffast-math would break isfinite checks); build with default flags.
Pass on the fixed revision requires the fixed commit to be built and the cephes extension rebuilt; a stale build would give a false failure on the fixed side.

No platform or sanitiser requirement is stated in the evidence; the defect is described as architecture-independent, but this is not confirmed, so if the NaN does not reproduce on the local machine, check the compiler and libm behaviour for overflow to infinity.
Dtype and precision of inputs are not stated; cephes.yn takes double precision scalars, which is assumed.

oracle.reference_source: Wolfram Alpha BesselY (cited in the PR as the cross-check for the negative asymptotic limit); the regression test itself compares to -np.inf exactly
oracle.why: The expected value is infinity, so the check is exact equality against -np.inf rather than a numeric tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On a24f7847e8cc, cephes.yn(500, 1) returns NaN because the original loop condition while (k < n) keeps iterating after the accumulated value has become infinite, producing inf minus inf style NaN. NaN == -np.inf is False, so assert fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the patch while (k < n && isfinite(an)), iteration stops once the value is infinite and cephes.yn(500, 1) returns -inf, so observed == -np.inf is True and the test passes.
